headline: The International Travel Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a travel companion how a local system works and check they understood, settle a dispute with a rental agent or host, report an incident or near miss without blame, make a clear emergency call, and write the day's report or claim in Spanish.

lessons.title: Teaching Your Group the Madrid Metro Card
lessons.objective: Explain step by step how to load, tap and transfer with a transit card, and say why each step matters.

words.note: In Madrid, the reloadable card used for metro, bus and Cercanías.
Common in Spain; you will also hear el torniquete.
Madrid Metro signs use Correspondencia for changing lines.
Extra fare at the airport stations; check the machine for the current price.
Madrid's commuter rail; Atocha is one of its main hubs.

words.en: First, top up the card at the ticket machine.
words.es: Primero, recarga la tarjeta en la máquina expendedora.
words.note: Informal tú command, normal between colleagues in Spain.

words.en: Then hold the card up to the turnstile reader.
words.es: Luego acerca la tarjeta al lector del torno.

words.en: The turnstile rejected it because you have no balance left.
words.es: El torno te la ha rechazado porque no te queda saldo.
words.note: Spain uses the present perfect for things that just happened.

words.en: There's a supplement to go to the airport; that's why it costs more.
words.es: Para ir al aeropuerto hay un suplemento; por eso cuesta más.

words.en: Don't throw it away, because it can be reloaded many times.
words.es: No la tires, porque se puede recargar muchas veces.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.

words.en: You're missing a step: before the turnstile, you have to top up.
words.es: Te falta un paso: antes del torno, hay que recargar.

words.en: Excuse me, does this machine take credit cards?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿esta máquina acepta tarjeta de crédito?
words.note: Formal, for station staff.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler who knows Madrid, and the AI is Diego, a colleague whose card was just rejected: explain step by step how to top up, tap and transfer, using primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have him explain it back and check it.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero recargas la tarjeta y luego pasas por el torno.
examples.en: First you top up the card and then you go through the turnstile.

examples.es: No tenías saldo; por eso el torno no se abrió.
examples.en: You had no balance; that's why the turnstile didn't open.

lessons.title: Why We Go Slow the First Day in Cusco
lessons.objective: Explain how altitude affects the body and why the group rests before a hard hike.

words.note: Andean word; also called el mal de altura.
Traditional Andean tea; it can show up on drug tests.
Also called Vinicunca or la Montaña de Siete Colores.

words.en: If you go up too fast, you get much more tired.
words.es: Si se sube muy rápido, uno se cansa mucho más.

words.en: Here you walk slowly on the first day.
words.es: Aquí se camina despacio el primer día.
Con la altura, se respira con más dificultad.

words.en: If your head hurts, tell me right away.
words.es: Si te duele la cabeza, avísame enseguida.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: If the symptoms continue, we go to the clinic.
words.es: Si los síntomas siguen, vamos a la clínica.

words.en: Doña Hilda, what do people recommend doing on the first day?
words.es: Doña Hilda, ¿qué se recomienda hacer el primer día?
words.note: Formal, to the owner; Doña plus first name shows respect.

words.en: Thank you, Doña Hilda, we'll take your advice.
words.es: Gracias, Doña Hilda, le hacemos caso.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Tomorrow we rest, and we'll do the hike another day.
words.es: Mañana descansamos, y la caminata la hacemos otro día.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend who planned the trip, and the AI is Paulina, who wants to hike Rainbow Mountain tomorrow, with owner Doña Hilda nearby: explain how altitude affects the body and why you rest first, using impersonal se and si + present (si se sube rápido, uno se cansa).

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (si se sube rápido, uno se cansa)

examples.es: Si se sube rápido, uno se cansa y le duele la cabeza.
examples.en: If you go up fast, you get tired and your head hurts.

examples.es: En Cusco se come ligero el primer día.
examples.en: In Cusco people eat light on the first day.

lessons.title: Showing a Companion the Room Safe and Passport Copies
lessons.objective: Give clear instructions for using a room safe and keeping passport copies, then check them back.

words.note: The passport page with your photo and number.
Mexican word; elsewhere riñonera.
Mexico uses la pila for small batteries.

words.en: Put it in the safe, not in your fanny pack.
words.es: Guárdalo en la caja fuerte, no en la cangurera.
words.note: Informal tú command, fine between travel companions.

words.en: Photocopy it and carry the copy in your wallet.
words.es: Fotocópialo y lleva la copia en la cartera.

words.en: Set your own code, not the factory one.
words.es: Ponle tu propio código, no el de fábrica.

words.en: Take a photo of the data page.
words.es: Tómale una foto a la página de datos.

words.en: Email it to yourself, so you have it in the cloud.
words.es: Mándatela por correo, así la tienes en la nube.

words.en: Don't leave it open when you go out.
words.es: No la dejes abierta cuando salgas.
words.note: Salgas is subjunctive after cuando for a future action.

words.en: Now you show me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora enséñamelo tú, paso por paso.

words.en: Excuse me, who has the master key for the safe?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿quién tiene la llave maestra de la caja?
words.note: Formal, to the guesthouse owner.

lessons.speaking: You are showing the AI, your travel companion Iker, how to use the room safe: give step-by-step commands like guárdalo, fotocópialo and no lo dejes en la mochila, explain where to keep a photo of his passport, then have him teach it back.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (guárdalo, fotocópialo, no lo dejes en la mochila)

examples.es: Guárdalo en la caja fuerte y ciérrala con tu código.
examples.en: Put it in the safe and lock it with your code.

examples.es: No lo dejes en la mochila; déjalo aquí.
examples.en: Don't leave it in your backpack; leave it here.

lessons.title: Read the Pharmacy Leaflet Before Anyone Takes a Dose
lessons.objective: Read a medicine leaflet aloud, explain its warnings, and confirm the dose with the pharmacist before use.

words.note: In Colombia you will also hear el inserto.
Common Colombian word for a pharmacy.

words.en: Wait, Gabriela, before taking anything, let's read this.
words.es: Espera, Gabriela, antes de tomar nada leamos esto.
words.note: Informal, to a companion.

words.en: It says here it can cause drowsiness.
words.es: Aquí dice que puede causar somnolencia.

words.en: It says here: don't drive after taking it.
words.es: Aquí dice: no manejar después de tomarlo.

words.en: Mr. Nelson, can it be taken with a sleeping pill?
words.es: Señor Nelson, ¿se puede tomar con una pastilla para dormir?
words.note: Formal, to the pharmacist.

words.en: What dose does the leaflet give for an adult?
words.es: ¿Qué dosis indica el prospecto para un adulto?

words.en: Do you have to take it after eating or on an empty stomach?
words.es: ¿Hay que tomarlo después de comer o en ayunas?

words.en: Don't mix it with your pill until he tells us.
words.es: No lo mezcles con tu pastilla hasta que él nos diga.
words.note: Informal; diga is subjunctive after hasta que.

words.en: Could you write it on the box for me, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo podría anotar en el empaque, por favor?
words.note: Formal and polite.

lessons.speaking: You are at the pharmacy counter with your companion Gabriela, and the AI is pharmacist Nelson: read the leaflet's warnings aloud, explain them, ask about taking it with her sleeping pill and confirm the dose, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de tomarlo, hay que leer el prospecto)

examples.es: Antes de tomarlo, hay que leer el prospecto.
examples.en: Before taking it, you have to read the leaflet.

examples.es: Hay que preguntarle al farmacéutico antes de mezclarlo con otra pastilla.
examples.en: You have to ask the pharmacist before mixing it with another pill.

lessons.title: Rental Car Return: A Scratch You Didn't Make
lessons.objective: Describe the car's condition at pickup and propose a fair solution to a damage charge.

words.note: Spain's everyday word for a car scratch; rayón is more Latin American.
Spain: picking up the rental car. Returning it is la devolución.
Spain: the amount you pay before insurance covers damage. Latin America says deducible.
Spain: the amount held on your card while you have the car.
Spain usage. Latin America says estacionamiento or parqueo.
In Spain, businesses must give you this form when you ask for it.

words.en: When I picked it up, the bumper already had this scratch.
words.es: Cuando lo recogí, el parachoques ya tenía este arañazo.
words.note: Preterite (recogí) for the single event, imperfect (tenía) for how things were.

words.en: Look, I took these photos in the parking lot before leaving.
words.es: Mire, hice estas fotos en el aparcamiento antes de salir.
words.note: Formal. Hacer fotos is the usual phrase in Spain.

words.en: Could we check the inspection sheet from the pickup?
words.es: ¿Podríamos revisar la hoja de inspección de la recogida?

words.en: The photos are from May 12, at 9:40.
words.es: Las fotos son del 12 de mayo, a las 9:40.

words.en: With all due respect, I don't agree with this charge.
words.es: Con todo respeto, no estoy de acuerdo con este cargo.
words.note: Formal and firm but polite.

words.en: Would you mind calling the office where I picked it up?
words.es: ¿Le importaría llamar a la oficina donde lo recogí?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you leave the deposit uncharged while they check it?
words.es: ¿Podría dejar la fianza sin cargo mientras lo revisan?

words.en: If we can't sort it out, could you give me the complaint form?
words.es: Si no lo resolvemos, ¿me da la hoja de reclamaciones?

lessons.speaking: You are returning a rental car, and the AI is Rodrigo, the agent at the Málaga airport desk: explain that the bumper scratch was already there with the preterite and imperfect (cuando lo recogí ya tenía…), show your pickup photos, and propose a fair check with ¿podríamos…?

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (cuando lo recogí ya tenía el rayón; ¿podríamos ver las fotos?)

examples.es: Cuando hice las fotos, el arañazo ya estaba allí.
examples.en: When I took the photos, the scratch was already there.

examples.es: ¿Podríamos comparar mis fotos con la hoja de inspección?
examples.en: Could we compare my photos with the inspection sheet?

lessons.title: Ferry to Colonia Sold Out: Comparing Other Routes
lessons.objective: Compare alternative routes by time, cost and risk, and announce the group's new plan.

words.note: Argentina: a ticket for a trip. ¿Cuánto sale? means how much is it.
A smaller passenger boat, like the ones that leave from Tigre.
Argentina's everyday word for a city bus.

words.en: Excuse me, is there a waitlist for the morning boat?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿hay lista de espera para el barco de la mañana?
words.note: Formal, to the ticket agent.

words.en: How much is the ticket for the afternoon boat?
words.es: ¿Cuánto sale el pasaje del barco de la tarde?

words.en: The route via Tigre is cheaper, but it takes almost twice as long.
words.es: La ruta por Tigre es más barata, pero tarda casi el doble.

words.en: The afternoon boat costs more than the bus-and-launch route.
words.es: El barco de la tarde cuesta más que la combinación con lancha.

words.en: Mateo, what time do you have to be at the airport?
words.es: Mateo, ¿a qué hora tenés que estar en el aeropuerto?
words.note: Informal. Argentines use vos: tenés, not tienes.

words.en: Relax, with this option you're going to have more time to spare.
words.es: Tranquilo, con esta opción vas a tener más margen.
words.note: Informal, to a worried friend.

words.en: Listen, here's the plan: we're going to go via Tigre.
words.es: Escuchen, este es el plan: vamos a ir por Tigre.
words.note: Ustedes command to the whole group.

lessons.speaking: You are leading a small group, and the AI is Carla, the ticket agent at the Buenos Aires ferry terminal: ask about the morning boat, compare the later ferry with the route via Tigre using más… que and menos… que, then announce the group's plan with vamos a and the future.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el autobús es más barato pero tarda más que el barco)

examples.es: La lancha desde Tigre tarda más que el barco directo, pero es más barata.
examples.en: The launch from Tigre takes longer than the direct boat, but it's cheaper.

examples.es: Vamos a tomar el colectivo y llegaremos a Tigre antes del mediodía.
examples.en: We're going to take the bus and we'll get to Tigre before noon.

lessons.title: Parking-Lot Fender-Bender with the Other Driver
lessons.objective: Narrate a minor collision clearly and exchange plate, policy and phone numbers accurately.

words.note: Dar marcha atrás means to back up.
Costa Rica usage; parquear means to park.
Costa Rica: the form the traffic officer gives each driver after a crash.

words.en: Officer Mora, my car was parked and the other one backed up.
words.es: Oficial Mora, mi carro estaba parqueado y el otro retrocedió.
words.note: Formal. Imperfect sets the scene, preterite tells the action.

words.en: It hit my rear door at 4:20 p.m.
words.es: Me pegó en la puerta trasera a las 4:20 p. m.

words.en: We didn't move the cars; they're where they ended up.
words.es: No movimos los carros; están donde quedaron.

words.en: Could you repeat the plate slowly, number by number?
words.es: ¿Me repite la placa despacio, número por número?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'll read you my policy number: 4471-2086.
words.es: Le leo mi número de póliza: 4471-2086.
words.note: Read long numbers in pairs: cuarenta y cuatro, setenta y uno…

words.en: Don Esteban, could you give me your phone number and your insurer's name?
words.es: Don Esteban, ¿me da su teléfono y el nombre de su aseguradora?
words.note: Formal. Don + first name is polite and common in Costa Rica.

words.en: Officer, can we move the cars now, or do we wait?
words.es: Oficial, ¿ya podemos mover los carros o esperamos?

words.en: I already called the rental company to let them know.
words.es: Ya llamé a la agencia de alquiler para avisarles.

lessons.speaking: You are the driver of a rental car, and the AI is Officer Mora of the traffic police in Liberia: tell what happened in the preterite (retrocedió, me pegó), read out the plate, policy and phone numbers clearly, and confirm the cars stay put until the officer says otherwise.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (placas, póliza, horas)

examples.es: Esteban dio marcha atrás y le pegó a mi puerta trasera.
examples.en: Esteban backed up and hit my rear door.

examples.es: Pasó a las 3:45 y anoté la placa BRT-512.
examples.en: It happened at 3:45 and I wrote down the plate BRT-512.

lessons.title: Saying No to a Boat Trip Without Life Jackets
lessons.objective: Refuse an unsafe offer politely but firmly and steer the group to a safer option.

words.note: Colombian word for a one-day outing, often to the islands.

words.en: No, thank you, sir; we're not getting on without life jackets.
words.es: No, gracias, señor; sin chalecos no nos subimos.
words.note: Formal, polite but firm.

words.en: Valeria, don't get on yet; look at the sea.
words.es: Valeria, no te subas todavía; mira cómo está el mar.
words.note: Informal. Negative tú command: no te subas.

words.en: I don't recommend we go with the sea like this.
words.es: No recomiendo que vayamos con el mar así.
words.note: No recomiendo que is followed by the subjunctive: vayamos.

words.en: Don't pay him anything yet, please.
words.es: No le pagues nada todavía, por favor.
words.note: Informal, to your companion.

words.en: Sir, why don't you have life jackets on board?
words.es: Señor, ¿por qué no tienen chalecos salvavidas a bordo?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Which pier do the licensed operators leave from?
words.es: ¿Desde qué muelle salen los operadores autorizados?

words.en: I'd rather pay more at the pier than take a risk here.
words.es: Prefiero pagar más en el muelle que arriesgarnos aquí.

words.en: Let's go to the pier and ask about a day trip with life jackets.
words.es: Vamos al muelle y preguntamos por un pasadía con chalecos.

lessons.speaking: You are traveling with a friend, and the AI plays Wilmer, a boatman on a Cartagena beach, and your companion Valeria: turn down the ride politely but firmly with negative commands (no te subas) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, then ask where the licensed boats at the pier leave from.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no subas; no recomiendo que vayamos)

examples.es: No te subas a ese bote sin chaleco, Valeria.
examples.en: Don't get on that boat without a life jacket, Valeria.

examples.es: No recomiendo que salgamos hoy con este oleaje.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we go out today with these waves.

lessons.title: Feedback for a Wine Tour Guide Who Rushed Us
lessons.objective: Give respectful, specific feedback to a guide and say what you hope changes for tomorrow's tour.

words.note: Common in Argentina for a tour or work schedule.
In Argentina, el micro is a tour or long-distance bus.
Agrees with the noun: la visita fue apurada.

words.en: Facundo, do you have a minute to talk privately?
words.es: Facundo, ¿tiene un minuto para hablar en privado?
words.note: Formal: usted keeps the feedback respectful.

words.en: Yesterday we felt the visit was very rushed.
words.es: Ayer sentimos que la visita fue muy apurada.

words.en: I understand the transport company changed your schedule.
words.es: Entiendo que la empresa de transporte le cambió el horario.

words.en: I hope we have time to eat lunch calmly tomorrow.
words.es: Espero que mañana tengamos tiempo para almorzar tranquilos.

words.en: I recommend that you let us know if the schedule changes.
words.es: Le recomiendo que nos avise si el cronograma cambia.
words.note: Formal: le recomiendo que + subjunctive.

words.en: Hopefully the tasting won't be so fast this time.
words.es: Ojalá que la degustación no sea tan rápida esta vez.

words.en: It would be good for us to take a break midday.
words.es: Sería bueno que hiciéramos una pausa a mitad del día.

words.en: Otherwise, your explanations about the vineyards were excellent.
words.es: Por lo demás, sus explicaciones sobre los viñedos fueron excelentes.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler on a two-day wine tour, and the AI is Facundo, the guide who rushed the group: give him specific, respectful feedback and say what you hope changes tomorrow, using espero que and le recomiendo que with the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (espero que, le recomiendo que)

examples.es: Espero que mañana el grupo pueda almorzar con calma.
examples.en: I hope the group can have lunch calmly tomorrow.

examples.es: Le recomiendo que llame a la empresa de transporte esta noche.
examples.en: I recommend that you call the transport company tonight.

lessons.title: Two Friends Arguing Over the Shared Hostel Bill
lessons.objective: Report what each side said, lay out the background facts, and help two friends agree on a fair split.

words.note: In Chile, la pieza is the usual word for a room.
Chile and Argentina say el vuelto for change given back after paying.
Informal Chilean slang: una luca = 1000 pesos.

words.en: Rocío said she had already paid for the first night.
words.es: Rocío dijo que ya había pagado la primera noche.

words.en: Tomás, you said you didn't have cash that day.
words.es: Tomás, tú dijiste que no tenías efectivo ese día.
words.note: Informal: tú between travel friends.

words.en: The ATM wasn't working, so Rocío paid for the taxis.
words.es: El cajero no funcionaba, por eso Rocío pagó los taxis.

words.en: Gonzalo, can you confirm what was paid and when?
words.es: Gonzalo, ¿nos puede confirmar qué se pagó y cuándo?
words.note: Formal: usted with the receptionist.

words.en: According to the receipt, Rocío paid the advance by card.
words.es: Según el comprobante, Rocío pagó el adelanto con tarjeta.

words.en: So each of you was supposed to pay half the room.
words.es: Entonces, cada uno debía pagar la mitad de la pieza.

words.en: Do you think it's fair to split the taxis equally?
words.es: ¿Les parece justo dividir los taxis en partes iguales?

words.en: Easy, it's not a big deal; we'll sort it out now.
words.es: Tranquilos, no es para tanto; lo arreglamos ahora.
words.note: Informal, to calm both friends.

lessons.speaking: You are a fellow traveler, and the AI plays Rocío, Tomás and receptionist Gonzalo: report what each friend said, lay out the background facts, and help them agree on a fair split, using reported speech (dijo que había pagado) and the imperfect (el cajero no funcionaba).

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Rocío dijo que ya había pagado; el cajero no funcionaba)

examples.es: Tomás dijo que el cajero no funcionaba esa noche.
examples.en: Tomás said the ATM wasn't working that night.

examples.es: Gonzalo explicó que Rocío había pagado el adelanto con tarjeta.
examples.en: Gonzalo explained that Rocío had paid the advance by card.

lessons.title: Keeping the Group Going on a Rainy Canyon Trail
lessons.objective: Encourage a tired group, commit to a clear plan, and follow the guide's call to turn back.

words.note: Common in Peru and Mexico; resbaladizo is also understood.
Use juntas only if the whole group is women.

words.en: Raúl is right; we'll return to the lodge on the same trail.
words.es: Raúl tiene razón; regresaremos al albergue por el mismo sendero.

words.en: Jimena, you can do it; we're going to make it together.
words.es: Jimena, tú puedes; lo vamos a lograr juntos.
words.note: Informal, warm encouragement.

words.en: Óscar, I understand you want to keep going, but today we won't climb.
words.es: Óscar, entiendo que quieras seguir, pero hoy no subiremos.

words.en: We'll go slowly, and nobody will be left behind.
words.es: Iremos despacio, y nadie se quedará atrás.

words.en: Beatriz, do you want my trekking pole for the descent?
words.es: Beatriz, ¿quieres mi bastón para la bajada?

words.en: Raúl, which way do you recommend we go down?
words.note: Formal: usted with the guide.

words.en: When we arrive, we'll change clothes and have something hot.
words.es: Cuando lleguemos, nos cambiaremos de ropa y tomaremos algo caliente.

words.en: Tomorrow we'll try again, only if Raúl says it's safe.
words.es: Mañana lo intentaremos otra vez, solo si Raúl dice que es seguro.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler in the group, and the AI plays guide Raúl and hikers Jimena, Óscar and Beatriz: back Raúl's call to return to the lodge, encourage the tired hikers, and commit to a clear plan using the future (regresaremos, llegaremos) and lo vamos a lograr juntos.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (llegaremos al refugio, lo vamos a lograr juntos)

examples.es: Llegaremos al albergue antes de que oscurezca.
examples.en: We'll reach the lodge before it gets dark.

examples.es: Lo vamos a lograr juntos, paso a paso.
examples.en: We're going to make it together, step by step.

lessons.title: One Change of Plan, Four Listeners in Granada
lessons.objective: Explain the same change of plan to a manager, a driver, a friend and a child, switching register each time.

words.note: In Spain, la carrera is the fare or trip in a taxi.
Informal Spain: darse un madrugón = get up very early.

words.en: Mr. Ortega, I'd like to ask you a favor about breakfast.
words.es: Sr. Ortega, quisiera pedirle un favor con el desayuno.
words.note: Formal: quisiera softens the request.

words.en: Would it be possible to have breakfast at 7:30 tomorrow?
words.es: ¿Sería posible tener el desayuno a las 7:30 mañana?
words.note: Formal softener for staff.

words.en: Paco, would you mind picking us up tomorrow at 8:00?
words.es: Paco, ¿le importaría recogernos mañana a las 8:00?
words.note: Formal: usted with the taxi driver.

words.en: How much would the ride to the Alhambra be at that time?
words.es: ¿Cuánto sería la carrera hasta la Alhambra a esa hora?

words.en: Hey, Inés, they've moved our visit to tomorrow morning.
words.es: Oye, Inés, nos han cambiado la visita a mañana por la mañana.
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend; Spain prefers han cambiado here.

words.en: Inés, do you feel like going up to the viewpoint this afternoon?
words.es: Inés, ¿te apetece subir al mirador esta tarde?
words.note: Informal, very common in Spain.

words.en: Lola, tomorrow we're getting up really early, okay?
words.es: Lola, mañana nos levantamos muy temprano, ¿vale?
words.note: Informal and simple for a child.

words.en: Will you help me set the alarm clock?
words.note: Informal: gives the child a small job.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler in Granada, and the AI plays manager Sr. Ortega, taxi driver Paco, your friend Inés and young Lola: explain that the Alhambra visit moved to tomorrow morning, using usted with softeners (quisiera, ¿sería posible?) for the adults and tú with Inés and Lola.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿sería posible?)

examples.es: Quisiera adelantar el desayuno, si no es molestia.
examples.en: I'd like to move breakfast earlier, if it's no trouble.

examples.es: Inés, ¿te viene bien salir a las 8:00?
examples.en: Inés, does leaving at 8:00 work for you?

lessons.title: Slip on the Pool Deck: Hotel Incident Report
lessons.objective: Narrate an injury incident in order with exact times and details for the hotel's report.

words.note: Marisa is a woman: la oficial. For a man: el oficial.
Mexican word for pool; piscina in most other countries.
Mexico: poolside or beach lounge chair.

words.en: At 5:00 p.m., we got out of the pool.
words.es: A las 5:00 de la tarde, salimos de la alberca.

words.en: While he was walking to the lounge chairs, Héctor slipped.
words.es: Mientras caminaba hacia los camastros, Héctor se resbaló.
words.note: Imperfect (caminaba) for the background, preterite (se resbaló) for the event.

words.en: The floor was wet and there was no sign.
words.es: El piso estaba mojado y no había ningún letrero.

words.en: A few minutes later, a staff member brought him ice.
words.es: Unos minutos después, un empleado le trajo hielo.

words.en: At 5:20, the hotel doctor examined him.
words.es: A las 5:20, el médico del hotel lo revisó.

words.en: In the end, the doctor recommended an X-ray.
words.es: Al final, el médico le recomendó una radiografía.

words.en: Officer, could you give me a copy of the report?
words.es: Oficial, ¿me podría dar una copia del reporte?
words.note: Formal: usted with the security officer.

words.en: Can I take photos of the floor before they dry it?
words.es: ¿Puedo tomar fotos del piso antes de que lo sequen?

lessons.speaking: You are Héctor's travel companion, and the AI is Marisa, the hotel security officer: give a step-by-step account of his fall with exact times, using a las 5:00, mientras, unos minutos después and al final, and ask for a copy of the report.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las cinco, unos minutos después, mientras, al final)

examples.es: Mientras Héctor caminaba por la orilla, yo estaba en el camastro.
examples.en: While Héctor was walking along the edge, I was on the lounge chair.

examples.es: Unos minutos después, llamamos a la recepción.
examples.en: A few minutes later, we called the front desk.

lessons.title: Gas Left On: A Near-Miss Talk Without Blame
lessons.objective: Talk through what almost happened without blaming anyone, and agree on new habits for the apartment.

words.note: The valve that cuts the gas (or water) supply.
If you smell gas, don't flip switches; follow the host's instructions.

words.en: We almost didn't notice the smell.
words.es: Por poco no nos damos cuenta del olor.
words.note: Por poco + present tense describes something that almost happened in the past.

words.en: If we hadn't smelled it, something serious could have happened.
words.es: Si no lo hubiéramos olido, podría haber pasado algo grave.

words.en: I opened the windows and didn't touch any switch, as the instructions say.
words.es: Abrí las ventanas y no toqué ningún interruptor, como dicen las instrucciones.

words.en: Relax, it's nobody's fault; it could have happened to anyone.
words.es: Tranquilos, no es culpa de nadie; le pudo pasar a cualquiera.
words.note: Informal, to roommates.

words.en: The knob looked off, but it wasn't all the way.
words.es: La perilla parecía cerrada, pero no estaba del todo.

words.en: Doña Gloria, could you explain how the stove knobs work?
words.es: Doña Gloria, ¿nos explica cómo funcionan las perillas de la estufa?
words.note: Formal: usted with the host.

words.en: Doña Gloria, where is the gas shutoff valve?
words.es: Doña Gloria, ¿dónde está la llave de paso del gas?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: How about we check the knobs before going out?
words.es: ¿Qué tal si revisamos las perillas antes de salir?
words.note: Informal suggestion among roommates.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest who smelled the gas, and the AI is Gloria, the host, with your roommates: explain what almost happened without blaming anyone, using casi, por poco and si no lo hubiéramos olido, podría haber..., and agree on new habits for the stove.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (si no lo hubiéramos olido, podría haber pasado algo grave)

examples.es: Por poco nos dormimos con el quemador abierto.
examples.en: We almost fell asleep with the burner on.

examples.es: Si no hubiéramos ventilado la cocina, podría haber sido peor.
examples.en: If we hadn't aired out the kitchen, it could have been worse.

lessons.title: Night Tremor: Phoning the Group and Front Desk
lessons.objective: Give short, clear phone instructions in an emergency and confirm the hotel's evacuation plan.

words.note: In Chile, temblor is a quake; terremoto is a very strong one.
Common on signs in Chile, marking where to wait during a quake.
Chile: internal phone number of a room or desk.
Standard loanword in Chilean hotels.

words.en: Are you OK in 512? Put your shoes on and wait.
words.es: ¿Están bien en la 512? Pónganse los zapatos y esperen.

words.en: Don't use the elevator, even if it seems to be working.
words.es: No usen el ascensor, aunque parezca que funciona.

words.en: If there's an aftershock, get down and protect your head.
words.es: Si hay una réplica, agáchate y protégete la cabeza.
words.note: Informal tú command to one companion.

words.en: Ignacio, what does the hotel's evacuation plan say?
words.es: Ignacio, ¿qué indica el plan de evacuación del hotel?
words.note: Formal: usted with hotel staff.

words.en: Do we wait in the room or go down now?
words.es: ¿Esperamos en la habitación o bajamos ahora?

words.en: Where is the nearest safe zone?
words.es: ¿Dónde queda la zona de seguridad más cercana?

words.en: If Ignacio gives the order, we'll go down the stairs together.
words.es: Si Ignacio da la orden, bajaremos juntos por la escalera.

words.en: Stay there; I'll call you back in 2 minutes.
words.es: Quédate ahí; te vuelvo a llamar en 2 minutos.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the group's organizer, and the AI is Ignacio, the night clerk, then your companions in rooms 512 and 514: confirm the evacuation plan and give short phone commands, using si + present (si suena la alarma, bajamos) and commands like quédate ahí.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone commands (si suena la alarma, bajamos por la escalera B; quédate ahí)

examples.es: Si suena la alarma, bajamos por la escalera de emergencia.
examples.en: If the alarm goes off, we go down the emergency stairs.

examples.es: Quédate lejos de la ventana y espera mi llamada.
examples.en: Stay away from the window and wait for my call.

lessons.title: Park Ranger Checks Our Galápagos Permits
lessons.objective: Present the group's documents formally and confirm the park's rules before the excursion.

words.note: Same form for a man: el guardaparque.
For a woman: la guía naturalista.
Common loanword; hacer snorkel means to go snorkeling.
Feminine noun, but el before stressed a: el área, las áreas.

words.en: Good morning, here are the group's transit cards.
words.es: Buenos días, aquí tiene las tarjetas de tránsito del grupo.
words.note: Formal: aquí tiene (usted).

words.en: And these are the entry fee receipts.
words.es: Y estos son los recibos de la tasa de ingreso.

words.en: According to the regulations, a distance of 2 meters is kept from the wildlife.
words.es: Según el reglamento, se mantienen 2 metros de distancia de la fauna.

words.en: Understood: touching or feeding the animals is not allowed.
words.es: Entendido: no se permite tocar ni alimentar a los animales.

words.en: Excuse me, is snorkeling allowed without a naturalist guide?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿se puede hacer snorkel sin guía naturalista?

words.en: I confirm that we will snorkel only with our guide.
words.es: Le confirmo que haremos snorkel solo con nuestro guía.
words.note: Formal: le confirmo.

words.en: Is using a flash allowed near the sea lions?
words.es: ¿Se permite usar flash cerca de los lobos marinos?

words.en: No trash is left at the visitor sites, correct?
words.es: No se deja ninguna basura en los sitios de visita, ¿correcto?

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI is Ana Lucía, the park ranger at the Santa Cruz dock: present the group's documents formally, read out the park rules with passive se (se revisan, no se permite), and explain your snorkeling plan and which rules you'll follow.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se revisan los permisos, no se permite tocar a los animales)

examples.es: Aquí se revisan las tarjetas de tránsito antes de embarcar.
examples.en: Transit cards are checked here before boarding.

examples.es: No se permite salir de los senderos señalados.
examples.en: Leaving the marked trails is not allowed.

lessons.title: Writing the Insurance Claim for a Stolen Camera
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal claim email that sets out the facts, the police report and the documents attached.

words.note: Standard insurance word for the event you are claiming for.
Common term in Peru for a store receipt.
Use el titular for a man.

words.en: I am writing to you to file a theft claim.
words.es: Me dirijo a usted para presentar un reclamo por robo.
words.note: Formal opening line for an email.

words.en: First, the camera was stolen in Miraflores.
words.es: En primer lugar, la cámara fue robada en Miraflores.

words.en: Afterwards, we filed the report with the police.
words.es: Posteriormente, presentamos la denuncia ante la policía.

words.en: Therefore, we request compensation according to the policy coverage.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicitamos la indemnización según la cobertura de la póliza.

words.en: Attached are the police report and a copy of Fernanda's passport.
words.es: Adjunto la denuncia policial y una copia del pasaporte de Fernanda.

words.en: According to the report, the theft happened at 3:15 p.m.
words.es: Según la denuncia, el robo ocurrió a las 3:15 p. m.

words.en: Could you tell me the deadline for sending the documents?
words.es: ¿Podría indicarme el plazo para enviar los documentos?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I look forward to your reply.
words.es: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
words.note: Formal closing; works for any gender.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI is insurer agent Sra. Quispe: write a formal claim for Fernanda's stolen camera, setting out the facts in order with en primer lugar, posteriormente and por lo tanto, and list your documents with adjunto.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, posteriormente, por lo tanto, adjunto)

examples.es: En primer lugar, el robo ocurrió en el lobby del hotel.
examples.en: First, the theft happened in the hotel lobby.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, le adjunto la boleta de venta de la cámara.
examples.en: Therefore, I am attaching the camera's sales receipt.

lessons.title: Moving the Airport Pickup by Phone and WhatsApp
lessons.objective: Leave a clear voicemail and send polite texts to reschedule a transfer and confirm the details.

words.note: Use el operador for a man.
Common word in Uruguay for a hired driver.
Valija is the usual word in Uruguay and Argentina.
Informal: me dejó en visto = he read it but didn't answer.
In Uruguay, a WhatsApp voice message is un audio.

words.en: Hi, Walter, I'm leaving you a message about tomorrow's transfer.
words.es: Hola, Walter, le dejo un mensaje sobre el traslado de mañana.
words.note: Formal voicemail opening.

words.en: They moved our flight up to 6:10 in the morning.
words.es: Nos adelantaron el vuelo a las 6:10 de la mañana.

words.en: Would it work for you to pick us up at 3:30?
words.es: ¿Le vendría bien pasar a buscarnos a las 3:30?
words.note: Formal. Pasar a buscar is the usual Uruguayan way to say pick up.

words.en: I would appreciate it if you called me back at this number.
words.es: Le agradecería que me devolviera la llamada a este número.

words.en: We are 7 passengers and we have 10 large suitcases.
words.es: Somos 7 pasajeros y llevamos 10 valijas grandes.

words.en: Silvana, could you confirm whether you have a bigger van?
words.es: Silvana, ¿podría confirmarme si tienen una camioneta más grande?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would there be any extra charge for the night rate?
words.es: ¿Habría algún recargo por la tarifa nocturna?

words.en: Perfect, that's settled; thank you very much for your help.
words.es: Perfecto, quedamos así; muchas gracias por su ayuda.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI is driver Walter's voicemail and then his dispatcher Silvana: leave a clear voicemail, then text Silvana to move the pickup earlier and ask for a larger van, using ¿le vendría bien…?, ¿podría confirmarme…? and le agradecería que…

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿le vendría bien?, ¿podría confirmarme?)

examples.es: ¿Le vendría bien a Walter venir a la entrada del hotel?
examples.en: Would it work for Walter to come to the hotel entrance?

examples.es: ¿Podría confirmarme la matrícula de la camioneta?
examples.en: Could you confirm the van's license plate for me?

lessons.title: Checkout Walkthrough and the Apartment Deposit
lessons.objective: Walk through the apartment with the owner, explain any damage, and agree on conditions for the deposit.

words.note: Vaso is a drinking glass; vidrio is glass as a material.
Common word in Spain for small damage in a rental.
Usual in Spain on bills and receipts.
Use el propietario for a man.

words.en: I'm sorry, Amparo, a glass broke on us last night.
words.es: Lo siento, Amparo, anoche se nos rompió un vaso.
words.note: Se nos rompió presents it as an accident, which is natural here.

words.en: How much would it cost to replace the glass?
Is 8 euros for the glass all right with you?
words.es: ¿Le parecen bien 8 euros por el vaso?

words.en: The stain on the cushion is coffee; I think it will come out.
words.es: La mancha del cojín es de café; creo que sale.

words.en: I would take the cover to the dry cleaner's today.
words.es: Yo llevaría la funda a la tintorería hoy mismo.

words.en: I'll pay for the glass, as long as you return the full deposit.
words.es: Pago el vaso, siempre que me devuelva el depósito completo.
words.note: Siempre que + subjunctive sets a condition.

words.en: As long as the cushion comes out clean, would you return everything?
words.es: Con tal de que el cojín quede limpio, ¿me devolvería todo?

words.en: Could you put that in writing for me, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo podría poner por escrito, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest checking out, and the AI is owner Amparo: walk through the flat with her, explain the broken glass and the stained cushion, and agree on the deposit using the conditional (pagaría, ¿costaría?) and siempre que / con tal de que with the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (siempre que, con tal de que)

examples.es: Yo pagaría el vaso, siempre que el resto del depósito se devuelva entero.
examples.en: I would pay for the glass, as long as the rest of the deposit is returned in full.

examples.es: Llevo el cojín a la tintorería, con tal de que usted esté de acuerdo.
examples.en: I'll take the cushion to the dry cleaner's, provided that you agree.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Cancelled-Flight Day in Mexico City
lessons.objective: Lead the group through a hard day: teach, rebook, check a medicine, call for help, and report.

words.note: ¿En qué sentido? asks which way the line runs.
In Mexico acetaminophen is usually called paracetamol.
In Mexico, cuarto is more common than habitación in speech.
Mexican usage; in Spain pendientes are earrings.

words.en: Rebeca, first top up the card and then tap it at the turnstile.
words.es: Rebeca, primero recarga la tarjeta y luego pásala por el torniquete.
words.note: Informal tú commands to a companion.

words.en: Lorena, could you rebook us on the next available flight?
words.es: Lorena, ¿podría reubicarnos en el próximo vuelo disponible?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Joaquín, don't take anything until we check it with the pharmacist.
words.es: Joaquín, no tomes nada hasta que lo revisemos con el farmacéutico.

words.en: Don Efraín, according to the label, how many hours apart can it be taken?
words.es: Don Efraín, según la etiqueta, ¿cada cuántas horas se puede tomar?
words.note: Formal. Let the pharmacist read the label to you.

words.en: If the fever doesn't go down, we'll take him to a doctor.
words.es: Si la fiebre no baja, lo llevamos con un médico.

words.en: Arturo, would you have a double room for tonight?
words.es: Arturo, ¿tendría un cuarto doble para esta noche?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'm writing to ask you to pick us up tomorrow at 7:00.
words.es: Le escribo para pedirle que nos recoja mañana a las 7:00.

words.en: In short, they cancelled the flight and we leave early tomorrow.
words.es: En resumen, cancelaron el vuelo y salimos mañana temprano.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI plays the people you meet in Mexico City: teach Rebeca the Metrobús, rebook with agent Lorena, check a fever medicine label with Don Efraín, book a room with Arturo and text the driver, using commands, ¿podría…?, the subjunctive and past tenses.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Lorena nos dijo que el vuelo se había cancelado por el clima.
examples.en: Lorena told us that the flight had been cancelled because of the weather.

examples.es: Joaquín, te recomiendo que descanses hasta que leamos bien la etiqueta.
examples.en: Joaquín, I recommend you rest until we read the label carefully.
